content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: heavier payments overtime plus wider chat deflection. It is predicted to lift service level to 81.0% over 09:45-15:15 for ₹10,782, the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target.","why":"This is a staffing problem, not a demand problem. Payments had 7 flu sick calls this morning against a usual 2.0 a day, leaving 13 agents on the phones against 18 planned. Volume is only 5.4% over forecast and handle time is close to plan, so the fix has to add capacity or take calls away. With no action, service level is predicted at 53.0% for the disruption window (payments 39.2%), with 11.8% of callers abandoning. R2 does both: it moves 2 cross-skilled agents across for 10:00-11:00, delays payments breaks by 45 minutes, offers overtime to 18 payments agents through 15:00, and deflects 20% of status, refund and balance enquiries to chat. The predicted result is 81.0% overall (payments 76.3%, general 87.2%), abandons down to 4.5%, and 87.6% for the rest of the day. There are no policy violations.","trade_offs":["Cost vs R1: R1 reaches a slightly higher 83.1% (general 91.3%, abandons 4.1%) but costs ₹11,322, which is ₹540 more than R2.","Cost vs P4: P4 is ₹1,704 cheaper at ₹9,078 but is predicted to fall just short of target at 79.0%.","The cheaper plans miss the target by a wide margin. P2 (₹6,468) is predicted at 76.0% and P3 (₹6,750) at 71.6%, and the no-cost rebalance P1 reaches only 56.1%.","Risk to the other queue: general should still improve on doing nothing, rising from 71.8% to 87.2%, even though it lends 2 agents for an hour. Payments remains below 80% on its own at 76.3%, so customers on that queue will still feel some impact."],"watch":"The 81.0% forecast depends on most of the 18 overtime offers being accepted, so confirm the take-up early. R2 clears the target by only 1 point, and fewer acceptances could push it below 80%. Also check that the chat deflection is actually moving status and refund enquiries off the phones. Watch for further flu absences in payments, since more sick calls would widen the gap."}
